owner-publishing.title: From Publish to the website
owner-publishing.subtitle: Follow the owner action. Preview uses the same handoff with a different target.
owner-publishing.footer: A successful workflow confirms its checks. Verify the edited page separately.

stages.title: Confirm and finish saving
stages.detail: The owner confirms Preview or Publish. The editor saves the latest draft before submitting it.

stages.title: Check permission and content
stages.detail: Check the session, tenant, write role, billing when enabled, fields, draft revision and source head.
stages.stop: If a check rejects the request, resolve it before publishing.

stages.title: Commit to the client repository
stages.detail: Write content.json to the selected branch. GitHub must accept the credential, branch policy and source head.
stages.note: Preview resets its branch to the checked live source. Publish writes a fresh live commit.

stages.title: Track the update and run the release

branches.title: Acknowledge the submission
branches.detail: Record the commit and publish ID, then return HTTP 202. This is not a deployment result.

branches.title: Build and deploy the site
branches.detail: The branch push starts checks, the site build, S3 uploads, CDN invalidation and the site's smoke check.

stages.note: These tasks overlap. GitHub can keep deploying if portal confirmation fails.

stages.title: Check the matching workflow
stages.detail: After acknowledgement, the browser polls while pending. The portal matches the content SHA, branch and workflow, even while the build is running.

stages.title: Read the result
stages.detail: See queued, building, preview ready, live or failed. An unavailable lookup keeps the last confirmed state.
stages.note: Preview ready means the review site is built; it does not promote the public site.

client-provisioning.title: Five stages to owner handoff
client-provisioning.subtitle: Hosting, site integration and owner handoff are separate stages.
client-provisioning.footer: Hosting resources alone do not mean the website or owner access is ready.

stages.title: Inspect and approve the plan
stages.detail: Read existing hosting and DNS, then review the exact changes. The default command only plans.
stages.stop: Make changes only after their effects are authorized.

stages.title: Create storage and validate HTTPS
stages.detail: Create the private, versioned S3 bucket. Request an ACM certificate and supply its DNS validation records.
stages.stop: If the certificate is still pending, stop and rerun after it is issued. Existing resources are detected.

stages.title: Connect delivery, DNS and monitoring
stages.detail: Set up CloudFront, origin access and the bucket policy. Add site DNS, health checks and alerts; record the resource map.
stages.note: Standard path: Cloudflare DNS and Route 53 health monitoring. Resolve conflicts or finish manual DNS before handoff.

stages.title: Connect the editable website
stages.detail: Provide the content contract and client build workflow. Configure the tenant's repository, credentials, branches, paths and URLs.

stages.title: Verify the handoff
stages.detail: Check the public site, preview target, owner access, saving and publication status. Verify monitoring delivery as well.
stages.note: Preview uses its own prefix and noindex. Noindex does not authenticate viewers.

portal-authorization.title: Who can change a website?
portal-authorization.subtitle: The server checks each gate. Continue only when it passes.
portal-authorization.footer: A visible button is not authorization. The server applies the same checks to direct API calls.

stages.title: Validate the session
stages.detail: Better Auth identifies the caller.

stages.title: Find an accessible tenant and source
stages.detail: Platform admins can access tenants. Other users must have a membership for this website.
stages.stop: 404: tenant, membership or connected content source is unavailable.

stages.title: Require an editing role
stages.detail: Allow a platform admin or a tenant editor/owner.

stages.title: Check whether editing is allowed
stages.detail: When billing is enabled, non-admin writes require canEdit. Admins bypass this check.
stages.stop: 402: editing is billing-locked. Disabling billing skips this gate.

stages.title: Validate the requested change
stages.detail: Apply field permissions, action validation, draft revision and source-head checks. Publish requires an explicit preview/live target.
stages.stop: Return the relevant field, conflict, target or rate-limit error.

stages.title: Save a draft or submit a publication

branches.title: Write Postgres
branches.detail: Store the draft. The public website does not change.

branches.title: Write the client repository
branches.detail: GitHub must accept the branch write. The client workflow deploys; the portal tracks its result.

stages.note: These are alternative actions. Save can retain an incomplete draft; publication requires valid content.

deployment-identity.title: How a release gets AWS permission
deployment-identity.subtitle: Passing CI, running a job and being allowed to write are different gates.
deployment-identity.footer: IAM checks each operation. A later denial does not undo earlier writes.

stages.title: Select an eligible release job
stages.detail: The repository's event and revision conditions choose the release and its runner.
stages.note: Portal CodeBuild runner permissions cover its connection and logs; deployment uses a separate role.

stages.title: Issue an identity token
stages.detail: The job requests an OIDC token using id-token: write. This permission does not grant an AWS action.

stages.title: Check the role's trust policy
stages.detail: Validate the token's issuer, audience and subject before issuing temporary deploy-role credentials.

stages.title: Authorize the operation
stages.detail: Check the requested action and resource against the applicable policies.
stages.stop: Denied action: that operation fails. Inspect any writes that already completed.

stages.title: Write and verify the release
stages.detail: Run the permitted S3, ECR, Lambda, SSM or CDN steps. Complete the application's own release checks.
stages.note: Credential exchange is permission evidence, not proof of human approval or a successful release.

portal-rollout.title: Release the portal container
portal-rollout.subtitle: This updates app.raizhost.com code. Owner content uses the client workflow.
portal-rollout.footer: A rejected release stays failed even if recovery restores a healthy previous image.

stages.title: Select the successful CI revision
stages.detail: Deploy the exact head SHA whose eligible push CI built the portal image.

stages.title: Prepare the release
stages.detail: Install and verify the reviewed deploy script. Apply only the allowlisted additive migrations.
stages.stop: Preparation failure stops the release before switching the container. Inspect completed preparation steps.

stages.title: Start the candidate image
stages.detail: Refresh the environment, pull the SHA-tagged image and start the candidate container.

stages.title: Check image identity and health
stages.detail: Confirm the expected image is running and the container is healthy.

stages.title: Accept the release or recover

branches.title: Accept the candidate
branches.detail: Record the last-good SHA, request best-effort CDN invalidation, and require terminal SSM Success.

branches.title: Try the previous image
branches.detail: Use a valid, distinct last-good SHA if available. Start it and check its identity and health. Keep additive migrations.

stages.note: These are alternative outcomes. No eligible image or failed recovery means recovery is unconfirmed.

publish-status.title: What a publication status means
publish-status.subtitle: Match the content commit, branch and workflow. A missed observation can skip an intermediate state.
publish-status.footer: Unavailable lookup: retain the last confirmed state. It is not a new success or failure.

stages.title: Submission recorded
stages.detail: The content commit and tracking row exist. The run may still be waiting to appear.
stages.note: Next confirmed state can be building, live or failed.

stages.title: The matching run is in progress
stages.detail: Checks, uploads and verification can still fail.
stages.note: Next confirmed state can be live or failed.

stages.title: The matching workflow succeeded
stages.detail: For preview-kind, this means preview ready. For live-kind, the workflow reports a live deployment.
stages.note: Verify the changed page separately. Workflow success proves only the checks that ran.

stages.title: A failure was confirmed
stages.detail: An unsuccessful run, confirmed absence timeout or rejected retry handoff/identity can produce failure.
stages.note: S3 may be partly updated. An eligible retry creates a new tracking row; terminal rows do not reopen.
